topic: time-zone handling in a scheduling service
old_rule: Every event start is stored as a UTC instant, and a recurring series repeats at a fixed interval counted in whole hours from that anchor instant, with the organizer's zone kept only as a display hint.
new_rule: Every event start is stored as a local wall-clock date and time with an IANA zone name, and a recurring series is a rule over local dates whose occurrences are converted to UTC instants only at expansion.

planted.text: There is no rebase job, and organizers receive no email around the spring and autumn clock changes.
Organizers do not have to edit a series after a clock change to keep it at its usual hour.
The gap between two occurrences is not a fixed count of hours, since a week that crosses a transition is an hour shorter or longer.
The zone comes from the organizer's choice in the event form rather than from a guess based on the network address of the request.
Reminder jobs are written to the shared job queue rather than registered as cron entries on the worker hosts.
This service does not materialise occurrences ahead of time, so an edit to a series touches a single row.
planted.licence: Some calendar products store each occurrence as a separate row as soon as a series is created.

planted.text: The import endpoint does not accept floating times and asks the user to pick a zone instead.
planted.licence: The iCalendar standard allows a floating time that carries no zone at all.

planted.text: The service therefore does not read zone rules from the host but ships its own pinned copy of the tz database.
planted.licence: The operating system zone files on a host can lag behind those releases by months.

planted.text: A reminder is never sent for an occurrence that has been cancelled or deleted.
When an event has no reminder setting, no notification is sent before it starts.
